question: On which river in India was the Somasila Dam built?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pennar river.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Somasila Dam is built across the Pennar (Penna) River in Nellore district, Andhra Pradesh. (सोमशिला बांध — पेन्नार नदी)

 

• It is a major irrigation and multipurpose project, forming part of the Telugu Ganga Project, and supplies water for irrigation as well as drinking purposes to Nellore and Chennai.

 

• The Pennar (Penner) River originates near Nandi Hills, Chikkaballapur district, Karnataka, and flows through Andhra Pradesh before draining into the Bay of Bengal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important dams on the Pennar river system include the Sri Sailam (on Krishna, not Pennar — often confused) and Gandikota Dam (on Pennar, called the "Grand Canyon of India").

 

NOTE

 

• Krishna river (Option 1): Major dams on the Krishna include Nagarjuna Sagar and Srisailam, not Somasila.

 

• Sabarmati river (Option 3): Flows through Gujarat/Rajasthan; the Dharoi Dam is built on it, not Somasila.

 

• Tapti river (Option 4): The Ukai Dam is the major dam on the Tapti river, in Gujarat.

question: Which theory describes the collective effects of changes in Earth's movements on its climate over thousands of years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Milankovitch theory.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Milankovitch theory (Milankovitch cycles), proposed by Serbian geophysicist Milutin Milanković, explains long-term climate change caused by cyclical variations in Earth's orbital eccentricity, axial tilt (obliquity) and precession. (मिलनकोविच सिद्धांत — पृथ्वी की गति और जलवायु परिवर्तन)

 

• These orbital variations occur over cycles lasting tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands of years and alter the amount and distribution of solar radiation (insolation) received by Earth.

 

• The theory is widely used to explain the timing of glacial and interglacial periods (Ice Ages) in Earth's climatic history.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The three Milankovitch cycles are eccentricity (~100,000 years), obliquity (~41,000 years) and precession (~26,000 years).

 

NOTE

 

• Plate tectonics theory (Option 1): Explains the movement of Earth's lithospheric plates, responsible for earthquakes, volcanism and mountain building — not climate cycles.

 

• Copernicus' heliocentric theory (Option 2): States that the Sun, not the Earth, is at the centre of the solar system; unrelated to climate change.

 

• Continental drift theory (Option 4): Proposed by Alfred Wegener, it explains the movement of continents from a single landmass (Pangaea), not climatic cycles.

question: How many times has India won the South Asian Football Federation (SAFF) Championship as of December 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 9 times.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India has won the SAFF Championship a record 9 times: in 1993, 1997, 1999, 2005, 2009, 2011, 2015, 2021 and 2023. (सैफ चैम्पियनशिप — भारत 9 बार विजेता)

 

• The 2023 SAFF Championship was held in Bengaluru, India; the Indian team (captained by Sunil Chhetri) defeated Kuwait in the final via a penalty shoot-out.

 

• India is the most successful team in the history of the tournament, which is contested among South Asian nations under the South Asian Football Federation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sunil Chhetri is India's most-capped player and the tournament's all-time leading figure; he later announced retirement from international football in 2024.

 

NOTE

 

• 5 times, 7 times, 6 times (Options 1, 2, 3): All understate India's actual tally of 9 titles as of December 2023.

question: Which of the following types of crops are sown after the end of the monsoon season?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rabi crops.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rabi crops are sown in October-December, after the retreat/end of the south-west monsoon, and harvested in March-April. (रबी फसल — मानसून के बाद बोई जाने वाली फसल)

 

• They require cool weather for growth and warm weather at the time of germination/ripening; examples include wheat, gram (chana), mustard and barley.

 

• The term "Rabi" is derived from the Arabic word for "spring", since these crops are harvested in spring.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kharif crops (e.g. rice, maize, cotton, jowar) are sown with the onset of the monsoon (June-July) and harvested in September-October.

 

• Zaid crops (e.g. watermelon, cucumber, muskmelon) are short-duration summer crops grown between the Rabi and Kharif seasons (March-June).

 

NOTE

 

• Zaid crops (Option 1): Grown in the short summer season between Rabi and Kharif, not after the monsoon.

 

• Kharif crops (Option 2): Sown with the arrival of the monsoon, not after it ends.

 

• Vital crops (Option 4): Not a recognised agricultural crop-season classification in India.

question: By which ministry of Government of India was the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana started?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Rural Development.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India. (दीनदयाल अंत्योदय योजना — ग्रामीण विकास मंत्रालय)

 

• It began as the Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY), was restructured as the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM) in 2011, and was renamed DAY-NRLM in November 2015, marking the birth centenary of Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay.

 

• The scheme aims to organise rural poor households into Self Help Groups (SHGs) and build sustainable livelihoods for them.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The urban counterpart, DAY-NULM (National Urban Livelihoods Mission), is implemented by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

 

NOTE

 

• Ministry of Home affairs, Ministry of Labour and Employment, Ministry of Corporate affairs (Options 2, 3, 4): None of these ministries administers the DAY-NRLM scheme.

question: How many types of writs can be issued by the Supreme Court to protect the Fundamental Rights of Indian citizens?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Five.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Article 32 (and Article 226 for High Courts), the Supreme Court can issue five types of writs to enforce Fundamental Rights: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari and Quo Warranto. (पांच प्रकार के रिट — मौलिक अधिकारों की रक्षा)

 

• Article 32 itself is a Fundamental Right and was described by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar as the "heart and soul" of the Constitution.

 

• Each writ serves a distinct purpose — e.g., Habeas Corpus ("to have the body") secures release from illegal detention, while Mandamus commands a public authority to perform its duty.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 226 empowers High Courts to issue the same five writs, but for a wider purpose — enforcement of Fundamental Rights and any other legal right.

 

NOTE

 

• Six, Four, Seven (Options 1, 2, 4): All state an incorrect count; the Constitution recognises exactly five kinds of writs.

question: What is the name of the centrally sponsored scheme related with literacy that was launched by the Government of India in March 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is New India Literacy Programme.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The New India Literacy Programme (NILP) — also known as ULLAS (Understanding of Lifelong Learning for All in Society) – Nav Bharat Saaksharta Karyakram — is a centrally sponsored scheme of the Ministry of Education for the period 2022-27. (नई भारत साक्षरता कार्यक्रम — नवभारत साक्षरता अभियान)

 

• It aims to cover non-literate persons aged 15 years and above and support the goals of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020.

 

• The scheme covers five components: Foundational Literacy and Numeracy, Critical Life Skills, Vocational Skills, Basic Education, and Continuing Education.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• NILP replaced the earlier Saakshar Bharat scheme and uses a volunteer-based teaching-learning approach, supported by a dedicated mobile app.

 

NOTE

 

• National Literacy Programme, India Literacy Programme, Bharat Padhega (Options 1, 3, 4): These are not the actual names of the Government of India's current literacy scheme.

question: Match the following musical instruments with the maestros who play them.
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• a. Santoor - iii. Pt Shiv Kumar Sharma: Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma is renowned for popularising the santoor as a classical concert instrument. (पंडित शिवकुमार शर्मा — संतूर वादक)

 

• b. Sitar - iv. Anoushka Shankar: Anoushka Shankar, daughter and disciple of Pt. Ravi Shankar, is an internationally acclaimed sitar player.

 

• c. Shehnai - i. Bismillah Khan: Ustad Bismillah Khan, a Bharat Ratna awardee, was the pre-eminent maestro of the shehnai.

 

• d. Sarangi - ii. Ustad Binda Khan: Ustad Binda Khan was a celebrated early-20th-century sarangi maestro who helped bring the instrument to the concert stage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known sarangi players include Ustad Sultan Khan and Pt Ram Narayan; other santoor exponents include Bhajan Sopori.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 pair the instruments with the wrong maestros — for instance, they wrongly assign Bismillah Khan to an instrument other than shehnai, or Pt Shiv Kumar Sharma to an instrument other than santoor.

question: In 2023, Gulab Chand Kataria became the Governor of which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gulab Chand Kataria, a veteran BJP leader from Udaipur, Rajasthan, was appointed Governor of Assam and took oath on 27 February 2023. (गुलाब चंद कटारिया — असम के राज्यपाल)

 

• He succeeded Jagdish Mukhi as the Governor of Assam.

 

• Before this appointment, Kataria was a long-serving Rajasthan legislator and had held the post of Rajasthan's Home Minister and Leader of Opposition in the Rajasthan Assembly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Governors are appointed by the President of India under Article 155 of the Constitution, usually for a five-year term at the President's pleasure.

 

NOTE

 

• Himachal Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Odisha (Options 1, 2, 3): Kataria was not appointed Governor of any of these states.

question: Match List-I (Name of the composition) with List-II (Writer).
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1-B, 2-C, 3-A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 1. Vande Mataram - B. Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay: Written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay in his novel Anandmath; it is India's National Song. (वंदे मातरम् — बंकिम चंद्र चट्टोपाध्याय)

 

• 2. Jana Gana Mana - C. Rabindranath Tagore: Composed by Rabindranath Tagore; it was adopted as India's National Anthem on 24 January 1950.

 

• 3. Ae Mere Watan Ke Logo - A. Pradeep: Written by Kavi Pradeep, this patriotic song was famously sung by Lata Mangeshkar in front of Pandit Nehru after the 1962 Indo-China war.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tagore is also the author of Bangladesh's national anthem "Amar Shonar Bangla", making him the only person to have written the national anthems of two countries.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 mismatch at least one composition with the wrong writer among Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, Rabindranath Tagore and Kavi Pradeep.

question: As per Olympic rules, in the third game, badminton players change ends when a side scores _____ points.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 11.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under BWF (Badminton World Federation) rules, a match is the best of three games, each played to 21 points. (बैडमिंटन — तीसरे गेम में 11 अंक पर छोर बदलना)

 

• In the third (deciding) game, players/pairs change ends as soon as either side reaches 11 points — this is meant to neutralise any positional advantage (e.g., lighting, air flow) for the remainder of the decider.

 

• In the first two games, players change ends only at the end of each game, not mid-way.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Each game uses the rally point system: a point is scored on every serve, games are played to 21 points with a 2-point lead required to win (capped at 30 points).

 

NOTE

 

• 13, 15, 12 (Options 2, 3, 4): None of these is the correct threshold specified by BWF rules for changing ends in the third game.

question: The loss of water in the form of water droplets from leaves of plants is called _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Guttation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Guttation is the loss of water in liquid form as droplets from the tips or margins of leaves, occurring through specialised pores called hydathodes. (गटेशन — पत्तियों से जल की बूंदों का रिसाव)

 

• It typically occurs during night or early morning, when high root pressure and high atmospheric humidity prevent water loss through normal transpiration.

 

• It is commonly observed in grasses and small herbaceous plants such as tomato and strawberry.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Guttation is distinct from transpiration, which is the loss of water in vapour form through stomata.

 

NOTE

 

• Pressure gradient (Option 1): A physics term for the difference in pressure across a distance; not a botanical process.

 

• Translocation (Option 3): The movement of manufactured food (sugars) through the phloem of a plant, not water loss.

 

• Plasmolysis (Option 4): The shrinking of a plant cell's protoplasm away from its cell wall due to loss of water in a hypertonic solution.

question: A _________________ is a cloud of dust and gas inside a galaxy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is nebula.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A nebula is a giant interstellar cloud of dust, hydrogen, helium and other ionised gases found within a galaxy. (नेबुला — गैस और धूल का बादल)

 

• Nebulae are often the birthplace of new stars, formed when gravity causes regions of the cloud to collapse and form protostars.

 

• Well-known examples include the Orion Nebula and the Eagle Nebula (home to the "Pillars of Creation").

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• A nebula can also form from the debris of a dying/exploded star (supernova remnant), such as the Crab Nebula.

 

NOTE

 

• Photosphere (Option 1): The visible outer surface layer of the Sun (or a star), from which light is emitted.

 

• Black hole (Option 2): A region of space with gravity so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape it.

 

• Chromosphere (Option 3): A layer of the Sun's atmosphere located just above the photosphere.

question: Who among the following was appointed, to the UN tax committee in July 2021, as a member for the 2021 to 2025 term?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rasmi Ranjan Das.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rasmi Ranjan Das, an officer of the Indian Revenue Service (IRS) serving in the Union Ministry of Finance, was appointed by the UN Secretary-General as a member of the UN Committee of Experts on International Cooperation in Tax Matters for the 2021-2025 term in July 2021. (रश्मि रंजन दास — यूएन कर समिति)

 

• He was the only Indian member among the 25 experts named to the committee for that term.

 

• The committee assists the UN Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) on matters of international cooperation in tax administration, particularly issues concerning developing countries.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The committee's work includes updating the UN Model Double Taxation Convention between developed and developing countries.

 

NOTE

 

• Vivek Singh, Vipul Bansal, TV Somanathan (Options 1, 2, 4): None of these individuals was named to the UN Tax Committee for the 2021-2025 term; TV Somanathan is a senior IAS officer who has served as India's Finance Secretary/Cabinet Secretary.

question: Who is the founder of modern micro finance ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Muhammad Yunus.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Muhammad Yunus, a Bangladeshi economist, is regarded as the founder of modern microfinance/microcredit. (मुहम्मद यूनुस — आधुनिक माइक्रोफाइनेंस के जनक)

 

• He founded the Grameen Bank in Bangladesh in 1983, which pioneered lending small, collateral-free loans to the rural poor, especially women.

 

• He was jointly awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006 (along with Grameen Bank) for efforts to create economic and social development from below through microcredit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Yunus authored the book "Banker to the Poor", describing the philosophy and growth of the Grameen Bank model.

 

NOTE

 

• VKV Rao, Rangarajan, YV Reddy (Options 1, 2, 3): These are Indian economists/former RBI Governors associated with Indian monetary policy and economic planning, not the founding of the modern microfinance movement.

question:
PC Mahalanobis is remembered as a major contributor of India's developmental path because he __________.

(A) set up Indian Institutes of Management located in different parts of India

(B) formulated the Second Five-Year Plan

(C) was the first Minister of Statistics and Programme Implementation
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only (B) is true.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis was an eminent statistician who founded the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) in 1931 and devised the "Mahalanobis Model", the economic strategy underlying India's Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61), which emphasised rapid industrialisation, particularly heavy industry. (पी.सी. महालनोबिस — द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना)

 

• Statement (B) is true — this is precisely his best-known contribution to India's development planning.

 

• Statement (A) is false — the Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs) were set up by the Government of India starting with IIM Calcutta in 1961; they were not established by Mahalanobis.

 

• Statement (C) is false — the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) was formed only in 1999, long after Mahalanobis's active career (he died in 1972); he never held the post of "Minister" of any ministry.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mahalanobis is also credited with founding the National Sample Survey (NSS) and developing the statistical measure known as the "Mahalanobis distance". India observes National Statistics Day on 29 June, his birth anniversary.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 are incorrect because each of them treats statement (A) — or (C) — as true, when both are factually false.

question: Who among the following was primarily an integral part of the Indian National Army (INA)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Subhas Chandra Bose.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Subhas Chandra Bose reorganised and led the Indian National Army (INA / Azad Hind Fauj) from 1943 onward, giving the famous call "Dilli Chalo" and the slogan "Jai Hind". (सुभाष चंद्र बोस — आज़ाद हिंद फौज)

 

• Bose formed the Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind Government) in Singapore in 1943, with the INA as its military wing.

 

• The INA was originally raised in 1942 by Mohan Singh and Rash Behari Bose with Japanese assistance, but it was under Subhas Chandra Bose's leadership that it grew into a major force for India's freedom struggle.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The INA had a women's regiment named the Rani of Jhansi Regiment, led by Captain Lakshmi Sahgal.

 

NOTE

 

• Rabindranath Tagore, Chittaranjan Das, Abanindranath Tagore (Options 1, 2, 3): None of these figures was part of the INA — Rabindranath Tagore was a poet/Nobel laureate, C. R. Das was a lawyer and Congress leader, and Abanindranath Tagore was a pioneering artist.

question: Which Clause of Article 20 incorporates the doctrine of double jeopardy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 20(2) of the Indian Constitution states that "no person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once" — this is the doctrine of double jeopardy. (अनुच्छेद 20(2) — दोहरे दंड से संरक्षण)

 

• Article 20 as a whole guarantees "Protection in respect of conviction for offences" and has three clauses.

 

• The doctrine ensures a person is not tried and punished twice for the same crime, protecting individual liberty against repeated prosecution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 20(1) protects against ex-post-facto laws (conviction only for an act that was an offence under the law in force at the time it was committed).

 

• Article 20(3) protects against self-incrimination (no person accused of an offence can be compelled to be a witness against himself).

 

NOTE

 

• 1, 4, 3 (Options 1, 2, 3): Clause 1 covers ex-post-facto laws, Clause 3 covers self-incrimination, and Article 20 has no Clause 4.

question: According to the Census of India-2011, which state has the largest gap between male and female literacy rates?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India, 2011, Rajasthan recorded the largest gender gap in literacy among Indian states, with a male literacy rate of about 80.5% against a female literacy rate of about 52.7% — a gap of roughly 28 percentage points. (राजस्थान — सबसे बड़ा लिंग साक्षरता अंतर)

 

• Rajasthan's overall literacy rate (about 66.1%) was also among the lower rates in the country in 2011.

 

• This wide gender gap reflects historically lower female school enrolment and higher dropout rates in the state.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kerala recorded the highest overall literacy rate (about 94%) in Census 2011, while Bihar recorded the lowest overall literacy rate.

 

NOTE

 

• Assam, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh (Options 1, 3, 4): Each of these states had a smaller male-female literacy gap in 2011 than Rajasthan.

question: Which of the following was the last dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aravidu dynasty.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Vijayanagara Empire was ruled by four successive dynasties: Sangama (1336), Saluva (1485), Tuluva (1503) and finally the Aravidu dynasty, which was the last dynasty to rule the empire. (अरविदु वंश — विजयनगर साम्राज्य का अंतिम राजवंश)

 

• The Aravidu dynasty was founded by Tirumala Deva Raya after the decisive Battle of Talikota (1565), which severely weakened the empire.

 

• The dynasty continued to rule in a diminished form until the empire's final decline around the mid-17th century.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Tuluva dynasty, which preceded the Aravidu dynasty, included the empire's most celebrated ruler, Krishnadevaraya, under whom Vijayanagara reached its zenith.

 

NOTE

 

• Sangam dynasty (Option 2): The first/founding dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire, established by Harihara I and Bukka Raya I.

 

• Saluva dynasty (Option 3): The second dynasty, founded by Saluva Narasimha.

 

• Tuluva dynasty (Option 4): The third dynasty, which included Krishnadevaraya; it preceded, but was not the last dynasty.

question: In MS Word, which feature allows you to create different headers and footers for odd and even pages in a document?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Different Odd & Even Pages.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In MS Word, under Header & Footer Tools > Design tab > Options group, checking the "Different Odd & Even Pages" option allows the user to design separate headers and footers for odd-numbered and even-numbered pages of the document. (अलग विषम व सम पृष्ठ — हेडर फुटर सेटिंग)

 

• This feature is commonly used in book-style/print layouts, where, for example, the odd pages might show the chapter title and even pages show the book title.

 

• It is accessed the same way as inserting a normal header/footer, via Insert > Header/Footer, and then enabling the option on the contextual Design ribbon.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The related "Different First Page" option lets the first page of a document/section have a unique header/footer (e.g. no page number on a title page).

 

NOTE

 

• Different First Page (Option 1): Creates a unique header/footer only for the first page, not separately for all odd/even pages.

 

• Page Breaks (Option 2): Forces content to start on a new page; it does not control header/footer content.

 

• Section Breaks (Option 4): Divides a document into sections that can each have independent formatting/headers-footers, but is not itself the odd/even header-footer feature.

question: _________ is a significant festival of the Parsi people who practice Zoroastrianism as it marks the birth anniversary of Zoroaster.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Khordad Sal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Khordad Sal is a major festival of the Parsi (Zoroastrian) community, celebrated to mark the birth anniversary of Prophet Zoroaster (Zarathustra). (खोरदाद साल — पारसी पर्व, जरथुस्त्र जन्मोत्सव)

 

• It falls on the sixth day of the Parsi calendar month of Farvardin and is observed with prayers at fire temples and festive gatherings.

 

• Zoroaster is the founder of Zoroastrianism, one of the world's oldest monotheistic religions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Jamshed-e-Navroz (Parsi New Year) is celebrated in honour of the legendary king Jamshed, while Pateti is a day of repentance and reflection observed just before the New Year.

 

NOTE

 

• Jamshed-e-Navroz (Option 1): Marks the Parsi New Year, not Zoroaster's birthday.

 

• Pateti (Option 2): A day of introspection and repentance, observed on the eve of the Parsi New Year.

 

• Gahambars (Option 4): Six seasonal festivals in the Zoroastrian calendar, associated with the seasons and creation, not specifically Zoroaster's birth anniversary.

question: Who among the following is a famous classical dancer?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sonal Mansingh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sonal Mansingh is one of India's most renowned classical dancers, trained in Bharatanatyam and Odissi, and a Padma Vibhushan awardee. (सोनल मानसिंह — प्रसिद्ध शास्त्रीय नृत्यांगना)

 

• She founded the Centre for Indian Classical Dances (CICD) in New Delhi and has been a nominated member of the Rajya Sabha.

 

• She has also received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for her contribution to classical dance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other legendary Odissi/Bharatanatyam exponents include Kelucharan Mohapatra, Yamini Krishnamurthy and Rukmini Devi Arundale.

 

NOTE

 

• Asha Bhosle (Option 2): A celebrated playback singer, not a classical dancer.

 

• Pratibha Ray (Option 3): An acclaimed Odia novelist and Jnanpith Award winner, not a dancer.

 

• S Janaki (Option 4): A renowned playback singer, particularly in South Indian languages.

question: In which year was tennis included in the Olympic games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1896.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tennis was one of the original sports contested at the first modern Olympic Games, held in Athens, Greece, in 1896. (टेनिस — 1896 एथेंस ओलंपिक)

 

• It featured in the Olympics continuously until 1924, after which it was dropped from the programme due to disputes over amateur status.

 

• Tennis was reintroduced as a full medal sport at the 1988 Seoul Olympics, and has remained part of the Games since.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tennis appeared as a demonstration sport in some of the Olympics between 1968 and 1984, before its full reinstatement in 1988.

 

NOTE

 

• 1948, 1935, 1927 (Options 1, 2, 4): None of these corresponds to tennis's actual introduction into the Olympic programme.

question: Which kind of computer security requires verifying the genuineness of the individuals or organisations that want to access a system?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Authentication.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Authentication is the computer security process of verifying the identity/genuineness of a user, device, or organisation attempting to access a system, typically using passwords, OTPs, biometrics or digital certificates. (प्रमाणीकरण — पहचान सत्यापन)

 

• It answers the question "Are you who you claim to be?" and is usually the first step, performed before authorization (which determines what an authenticated user is permitted to do).

 

• Authentication is one of the core pillars of information security, alongside confidentiality, integrity and availability.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Multi-factor authentication (MFA) combines two or more independent credentials (something you know, have, or are) to strengthen identity verification.

 

NOTE

 

• Non-repudiation (Option 1): Ensures a party cannot deny having performed an action, such as sending a message or making a transaction.

 

• Availability (Option 2): Ensures that systems and data remain accessible to authorised users whenever needed.

 

• Confidentiality (Option 4): Ensures that information is not disclosed to unauthorised parties.
